01 — Mindset
How I think
The operating system of a builder

I believe the most powerful thing a developer can have isn't a stack — it's a point of view.

Good software isn't shipped. It's composed — like music, like film.

I don't separate design from engineering. I don't separate the product from the story. Everything is one system.

// Principle 01

Build for the human, not the spec. Every pixel is a decision. Every interaction is a conversation.

// Principle 02

Chaos is not the enemy of creativity — it's the fuel. I built my best work on moving buses and between deadlines.

// Principle 03

Speed is a feature. So is restraint. The art is knowing when to ship and when to sit with the discomfort of not being done.

// Principle 04

Identity is infrastructure. The way you think is the architecture of everything you build.

04 — Process
How I work

How the
work gets made.

01_
Obsessive Research

Before a line of code, I study the user, the space, the feeling. I want to understand what the thing should feel like before I know what it does.

02_
System Architecture

Everything is designed as a system first. Components, flows, states. I think in graphs, not screens — because real products live in time, not in Figma.

03_
Build in Motion

I build fast and break often. Real environments, real constraints. Some of my best code was written in transit — pressure clarifies thinking.

04_
Cinematic Polish

The last 20% is where the magic lives. Motion, pacing, emotional tone. I stay until the product doesn't just work — it resonates.

05 — World

Beyond
the screen.

01 / Urban Explorer
Cities as systems

I'm drawn to urban environments — not just aesthetically but structurally. How people move, how spaces breathe, how density creates energy. Every city I visit teaches me something about product design.

02 / Cinephile
Film as a reference system

Cinema is my design school. How Villeneuve uses space. How Wong Kar-wai uses time. I study frames and pacing the way others study components. Every interface I build has a director's cut in my head.

03 / Reader
Books as architecture

Philosophy, systems thinking, design theory. I read the way I code — looking for patterns, principles, the underlying grammar. Nabokov taught me more about UX than any course.

04 / Observer
Noticing as practice

I watch how people interact with interfaces in the wild. The hesitation before a button. The relief after a successful form submit. Observation is my research method. Empathy is my stack.

05 / Dresser
Fashion as visual language

Style is intentional communication. I think about what I wear the way I think about UI — hierarchy, contrast, restraint. Presenting yourself is designing yourself.

06 / Night thinker
Solitude as signal

My best ideas arrive at night, in stillness — when the noise collapses and the signal becomes clear. I protect that time. It's not isolation. It's incubation.

Night mode
Solitude is productive silence.

Discipline is a form of self-respect.
